pipeline.title: Follow one wave through construction
pipeline.description: See where its budget ends and later changes begin.
pipeline.intro: Generate an Ancient Egypt level, then inspect one wave. Type selection, budget filling, final reservation, instruction levels, and the one-per-level leader attempt all contribute to the result.
pipeline.entitiesCaption: Each instruction uses its sampled level and the Endless health reference. The HP subtotal assumes neutral creation modifiers and successful placement.
pipeline.instructionsCaption: Each tile is one spawn instruction. Its cost is an input to construction, not its health.
pipeline.typesCaption: The basic type and four chosen pool entries become the filler’s active types.

explain.inputs: The displayed level supplies the common count and point formulas. Egypt supplies its own basic type and zombie pool.
explain.budget: The selected wave starts on the base progression. A regular flag boundary or final wave applies one ×2.5 multiplier.
explain.types: Four pool entries are selected by index without replacement. The basic type is added separately. The seed generates a repeatable level.
explain.fill: The final wave first reserves strictly affordable unseen types. Weighted filling then spends the remaining budget, accepting exact matches. Earlier waves determine which types are still unseen.
explain.extra: One level-wide chance can assign a leader to one wave. Its type is drawn by weight from selected types costing more than 100. Its cost is outside the ordinary budget.
explain.world: Egypt has no extra world designer here. Other worlds can now replace instructions or append independent actions; Chapter 3 follows those changes.
explain.flag: A flag/final wave receives a separate flag-zombie action unless suppressed. It has its own placement spacing and is outside the ordinary budget.
explain.entities: Each instruction has a sampled level. This calculation uses the adopted ten-level Endless health reference and applies the leader multiplier separately.
explain.placement: This view assumes successful placement for the generated Egypt roster. Chapter 5 lets you supply occupied rows and inspect rejection or relocation.
explain.snapshot: This is the ordinary action’s calculated HP subtotal under the stated assumptions. The game samples all eligible current-wave entities after every action returns, including an eligible flag entity.

pipeline.noLeaderAttempt: This level is below the extra-entry threshold of 4.
pipeline.leaderOutcome: One leader roll for this level: {roll} out of 100, successful below {threshold}. Assigned wave: {wave}.
pipeline.separateFlag: Separate flag action: {name}. Its entity level and health are resolved separately and are not included in this subtotal.
pipeline.reservationDetail: The final pass reserved {n} types that had not appeared in earlier budget-paid rosters.
pipeline.subtotalDetail: Per-entity conversion and float32 sum; separate flag action excluded

reservation.title: The final-wave inclusion pass
reservation.description: Change the unseen types and watch reservation consume the budget.
reservation.intro: These five active Egypt types are already selected. Mark which have never appeared, then follow the ordered reservation pass and the ordinary filler that runs afterward.
reservation.drawn: The filler makes a weighted draw
reservation.passDetail: {name}: cost {cost}, remaining {before}. The reservation requires cost < remaining. The new balance is {after}.
reservation.fillDetail: {name}: cost {cost} is affordable at {before}, including an exact match. This draw leaves {after}.
reservation.startDetail: The checked entries are visited in the displayed order. Earlier accepted reservations change the balance for later entries.
reservation.empty: No instruction has been inserted yet.
reservation.explanation: A skipped reservation does not remove a type from ordinary filling. The filler rebuilds its bag using cost ≤ remaining and positive Weight.

jam.title: Inside the music schedule
jam.description: Choose a level, inspect each music wave, and replay its replacements.
jam.intro: Generate an Eighties roster and music schedule from a repeatable example seed. Choose a music wave to follow its removals and replacements.
jam.selectedDetail: {n} distinct music types selected. The first event is on player-facing wave {first}. Each later event may choose the same music again.
jam.eventDetail: Replace {n} instructions. Endpoint draws: {first} and {second}; α = {alpha}. The next event is {spacing} waves later.
jam.beforeDetail: The music event and one replacement type have been chosen. The existing instructions have not been changed yet.
jam.removeDetail: Remove instruction {n}, save its level {level}, move the last instruction into its slot, then shorten the vector. The next removal samples the changed vector.
jam.appendDetail: Append a new {type} instruction using a saved level. Its leader marker is false; the removed instruction’s other fields are not copied.
jam.diagram: Animated instruction replacement with saved levels
jam.savedLevels: Removed instructions: only their levels are carried forward
jam.inputDetail: The input roster is generated by pool selection, weighted filling, final-wave reservation, per-instruction level draws, and a level-wide leader attempt. Jam then removes and appends instructions while retaining their levels. A new seed regenerates both parts.
jam.subsetTrace: How the distinct music subset was selected
jam.subsetExplanation: Draw repeatedly from the eligible music list. ✓ adds a new type; ↻ discards a duplicate while still consuming the random draw. Event choices later draw from the completed subset with repeats allowed.
jam.budgetDetail: Budget {budget}; {remaining} unspent; {reserved} final reservations; {leaders} extra leaders before music replacement.

portals.title: A portal, from queue to closure
portals.description: Inspect every family list and step through emission and removal.
portals.intro: A Modern event creates a portal action. Follow one resulting portal: it copies four family slots, shuffles them, emits children on its own clock, and remains a victory blocker until removal.
portals.parameters: Inspect the Modern event parameters at this level
portals.unusedCount: Computed count that is not forwarded
portals.parameterDetail: These are the possible endpoint-interpolation results. Each event makes fresh draws. Portal family/row choices and endpoint draws use distinct streams; the queue shuffle is an imported C++ operation.
portals.clearChildren: All emitted children have been cleared
portals.blockedPortal: Completion is blocked by the portal itself, even if its queue or the lawn is empty.
portals.blockedChildren: The portal is gone, but its surviving children still block completion.
portals.clear: Neither this portal nor its emitted children block completion now. Other level predicates still apply.
portals.orderDetail: The library shuffle permutes every family slot, including duplicates, from the selected stream position. Each step supplies an update or animation callback. Timing controls set the opening time, first offset, and later interval.

stages.closing: Next due check finds the empty queue

explain.copy: The ordinary action leaves the runtime count/range overrides untouched. Every slot is copied, including duplicates.
explain.shuffle: Reordering changes when each slot is consumed. It does not deduplicate names or shorten this four-slot list.
explain.opening: A first deadline is requested from the creation time. Emission also waits for opening to finish; an early deadline alone is insufficient.
explain.open: The portal can emit once both the opening-state gate and the requested deadline permit it.
explain.emit: A due update consumes one slot and creates its child with marker -5. The selected interval is added to the previous deadline, even for a late update or the final child. An empty queue starts closing only at a later due update.
explain.closing: At the next due emission check, the empty-queue branch requests the closing state and starts the close animation.
explain.removed: The animation-completion callback requests removal. Only now does the portal’s own resolvable-object blocker disappear.

steam.title: Smoke and pipeline clocks
steam.description: Compare fixed board positions, smoke clearing, and blocked transport.
steam.perPass: per selected cell target / damage pass
steam.board: Five-row Steam board and fixed module positions

smokeExplain.0: The alert deadline is start + {alert}s. The first roar deadline is independently start + {start}s. AlertTime is not subtracted from StartTime.
smokeExplain.1: At the first alert deadline the hole plays first_alert, then waits for the already-set roar deadline.
smokeExplain.2: At start + {start}s the first_roar animation is requested. Its completion event, not the request itself, activates damaging smoke.
smokeExplain.3: The smoke remains active. Use the update controls to inspect its strict accumulator > 1 damage gate. There is no automatic five-second expiry here.
smokeExplain.4: A traced blow_off or absorb path starts clearing. The cooldown begins when its removal animation completes.
smokeExplain.5: The removal event sets the next alert to clearing time + {cooldown}s, and the next roar to clearing time + {nextRoar}s, before any extra delay.
smokeExplain.6: The next alert plays alert or block depending on the retained blocker reference. The later roar deadline remains separate.
smokeExplain.7: The roar starts again. Only its completion returns the hole to the active damage state.

steam.onePass: Each update uses the chosen delta once; changing it leaves earlier updates intact. An accumulator strictly greater than 1 executes one pass and subtracts 1. Each of the nine cells selects one plant target; stacked layers are not all damaged independently.
steam.atExit: The entity uses the exit position
steam.pipeDetail: The same {count} entities are retained. Their underground deadline is t + {under}; completion requires time > {complete}. Multiple entities can be in flight together.
steam.deniedDetail: This example admits runtime small entities through an existing pipeline. Medium/large entities do not pass its size gate. Other native capability and state gates also apply.
steam.notPerZombie: not multiplied by the transported count
steam.countsInHealth: Included by the wave-health state filter
steam.positions: Player-facing positions: smoke holes use column 6 and rows 2 onward; pipes run from column 7 to column 5, starting in row 1. The scene uses the first pipeline for the transport example.
steam.noSmoke: No smoke holes at this level
steam.noSmokeDetail: The setup produces an empty smoke module. Choose a level from 34 onward to follow a hole’s lifecycle.

strength.title: From a level request to health and damage
strength.description: Inspect the level curve, residue test, and separate health multipliers.
strength.intro: The displayed Endless level L selects an instruction level. The created entity then resolves its own effective level ℓ and looks up separate health and attack multipliers.
strength.curve: The float32 requested-level curve across ordinary levels
strength.residueDetail: Gold marks the {n} residues that select upper level {upper}. The other residues select {lower}. The outlined cell is this example’s chosen residue.
strength.separateDetail: The module-override control supplies an effective level after creation modifiers. With no override, this example uses the requested instruction level.
strength.barLegend: Green is body health; gold is helmet health. Both use the health-table multiplier, then neutral leader strengthening when enabled.
strength.missingDetail: The bundled table has no row 6–10. Its lookup returns multiplier 1 for a missing row. This control shows that lookup; an effective server-supplied table can contain other rows.
strength.leaderDetail: Combined health changes from {before} to {after}. Leader marking does not directly change the attack multiplier. These types use fixed EatDPS; EatDPSRatio types have a separate indirect health-to-damage path. Each control change compares fresh entity setups.
strength.reportedDetail: Health uses the ten-level Endless reference. Leader marking applies its health multiplier separately.
strength.healthReportDetail: Base getter: float32 body + helmet, then signed int32 conversion. This reporting step leaves the stored HP unchanged.
strength.bundledDetail: This comparison uses the five-row DangerRoom table and the native bite formula, with neutral modifiers.
strength.attackUnmapped: The bite formula requires the separate AttackLevel input.

placement.title: Rows, history, and final placement
placement.description: Replay row choices and follow the same zombie through placement hooks.
placement.historyIntro: Choose the next sampled row, or load a two-choice example. The bars show the weights for the following draw. Scrubbing the sequence reconstructs both history counters.
placement.recurrence: For every eligible row, increment both a and b. For the chosen row, copy the incremented a into b, then set a = 0. The counters stay attached to this sampled row through later relocation.
placement.zeroDetail: The native scan accepts draw ≤ cumulative weight and retains zero-weight records. At exactly zero, its first record can pass even with zero weight. The row-choice controls above exercise positive-eligibility choices; the isolated native endpoint is a separate boundary case.
placement.hooksIntro: Track one newcomer through the provisional row, jitter, the base event, and its subclass hook. Occupied rows represent other same-class objects still present in the Board list.
placement.circle: An active circle accepts this newcomer
placement.board: Placement sequence with retained sampled-row history

hookStages.4: Finish placement or reject the newcomer

hookExplain.0: The weighted sampler records a choice in row {row}. This history is already committed before the later hooks.
hookExplain.1: The action’s spacing pass writes X/Y/Z and then invokes the placement hook. The batch already exists in the Board list.
hookExplain.2: An accepting Ghost Horse circle writes column 9, row 3. Without that callback, the provisional position remains.
hookExplain.3: Fisherman excludes itself from the same-class scan. King includes itself, so its own current row is removed too. Gold rings show the remaining candidates.

placement.retainedRow: The current row remains available and is retained: row {n}.
placement.shuffledRow: The current row is unavailable. A draw among the remaining candidates places the newcomer in row {n}, at the last column.
placement.rejectedKing: No candidate remains. The normal King path enters ZS_Die. It does not retry, refund the instruction, or remove an older King.
placement.rejectedFisher: No candidate remains. The normal Fisherman path dispatches removal immediately. Board-list erasure happens separately, and the ordinary loot path remains reachable.
placement.hookCaption: The provisional row and jitter are inputs. Relocation shuffles the remaining rows from the selected library-stream position. The original row keeps its history contribution.
placement.ordinaryHook: This ordinary type has no King/Fisherman occupancy scan. Its position after the base event is retained.

timing.title: What makes the next wave start?
timing.description: Compare capped HP reports, normal timing, and manual taps during a wave warning.
timing.views: Wave health, warning, and completion views
timing.intro: Enter the HP accumulator for other eligible current-wave entities, plus an optional newcomer that can be rejected before the snapshot. A later decrease changes that accumulator before it is converted to the reported integer. These are editable rule inputs, independent of the point budget.
timing.reject: Reject the optional newcomer before H₀
timing.timeline: Health event and alternative wave-advance timelines
timing.guardFormula: For current wave {wave}: {wave} mod {spacing} = {result}. The regular-boundary guard compares this with {boundary}; it does not independently guard every final wave.
timing.announcementDetail: The normal path reaches its first gate at {gate}s, then shifts deadline {old}s to {next}s for the announcement.
timing.trackedDetail: This tab follows the current wave through its first advance. It uses entered accumulator values and one health-loss event. The construction view separately calculates per-entity truncation and sequential float32 summation. The warning tab follows the state left by a manual tap.
timing.completionIntro: Completion combines several independent conditions. Change them directly to see why an empty lawn, a finished schedule, and an empty portal queue can produce different answers.
timing.closingPortal: Last child gone, portal is closing

conditions.portalGone: The portal object has been removed

timing.completionDetail: This panel supplies the listed predicate outcomes. The entity-clear predicate applies the exact exceptions described in the article; it does not substitute body HP > 0 for its native filters.
timing.eligibleHp: Other eligible HP before integer conversion
timing.saturationDetail: H₀ is capped at {cap}. H(t) uses the same conversion, so remaining health above this cap still reports the cap and cannot meet the smaller threshold. The health-loss input changes the entered accumulator before conversion.

loot.title: From planned counts to actual carriers
loot.description: Follow plant-food quotas, cost-weighted loot tags, and saved schedules.
loot.quotaIntro: An eligible setup row has MinLevel ≤ L. The highlighted flag row is one actual seeded choice among all eligible rows; the food bounds take minima across the entire eligible set.
loot.allocationDetail: Give one unit to each regular flag boundary in order while stock remains. After that pass, place any remaining units on random waves; a wave can receive more than one. A short final wave is not inserted into the regular-boundary pass.
loot.carrierIntro: The quota and ordered instructions are explicit inputs. Follow the property test, consumption, runtime class gate, and later pickup request as separate steps.

examples.2: Cowboy basic first: request consumed earlier

loot.canDrop: Later loot gates permit a pickup

carrierStages.3: Apply the runtime marker gate to instruction 1
carrierStages.6: Apply the runtime marker gate to instruction 2

loot.carrierStart: No random carrier draw occurs here. Requests are offered in instruction order until the quota is consumed.

carrierPhases.0: read CanSpawnPlantFood; false skips without consuming.
carrierPhases.1: a true property consumes one unit if any remains, before marker acceptance.
carrierPhases.2: the DangerRoom Gargantuar class gate can reject a consumed request; no refund follows.

loot.dropDetail: Accepted markers create pickups only if m_canDropLoot, the unprocessed flag, and mode gates permit the later event. Collection into inventory is a further operation.
loot.tagsIntro: These are three individual instructions, including the independent flag spawner. Loot uses their WavePointCost as weight. Compare the flag’s nonzero cost with its ordinary-filler Weight of zero.
loot.tagsDetail: A tagged instruction leaves the next bag. The example list uses codes 1, 2, and 3 in order; code 3 is named Diamond but this dispatcher requests coin_gold. Plant-food eligibility does not select these tags.
loot.scheduleIntro: Follow one saved UniqueId record across planning calls. The phase and count controls supply the random outcomes; holding them fixed makes the strict time comparisons visible.
loot.scheduleDiagram: Saved loot schedule with planning-length marker
loot.scheduleDetail: Each call adds {length} length units. New periods use phase {phase} and count {count} here. An open circle is a scheduled drop; filled circles are drops already emitted. ∞ is the no-pending-drop sentinel.

announcement.intro: Compare two transitions before a flag or final wave. The controls supply a current deadline, an optional tap, the next interval, and a time when the new wave clears. Automatic next-wave is off in this comparison.
announcement.deadlineInput: Current deadline after the HP check (seconds)
announcement.window: The button is available from {visible}s. Without an earlier tap, the pre-spawn warning runs from {from}s to {to}s.
announcement.unavailable: The entered tap falls outside the button’s available interval, so it does not apply.
announcement.timeline: Normal timeout and manual request, with warning, wave start, clearance, and following transition
announcement.legend: Gold shows the pre-spawn warning. The lower bar begins when the wave spawns: green uses normal timing, purple retains the warning state. The dashed marker is the entered clearance time. The bar ends at the next advance or manager-finalization attempt.
announcement.finishDetail: Finished state; entity clearance is checked separately
announcement.anotherUpdate: Then one more normal update; its duration is not specified
announcement.retainedEffect: The wave clears at {clear}s. In state 2, clearing does not accelerate the fresh deadline at {deadline}s, and the normal button-show logic is omitted. The timer still governs the next transition.
announcement.timedEffect: State 1 runs the normal health and button checks. Clearing can bring the deadline forward, subject to the four-second minimum.
announcement.completionBoundary: For the final wave, victory also requires the entity-clear predicate. A retained warning state needs another normal update after the finalization attempt; no extra scheduled wave is created.
announcement.scope: All times are game-clock inputs. At an exact boundary this comparison evaluates the timed update before the tap.

evolution.title: Follow an Evolution activation
evolution.description: Follow actual candidate selection, shared shuffle consumption, and deferred replacements across a 3×3 region.
evolution.lily: Lily Pad stage virtual returns true
evolution.inputNote: The grid shows plant anchors. Target order and planting-check results are scenario inputs. The selected stage applies the base stage rule; Lily Pad has its own supplied virtual result.
evolution.inspect: Inspect a cell to follow its selection
evolution.noCandidate: No candidate; this target stays in place.
evolution.checkNote: Selection excuses reason 79. The final check excuses nothing. Other candidates use empty blocking-reason sets in these examples.
evolution.retained: The original level is carried into the replacement.
evolution.bonusLevel: The bonus-level minimum starts at 1. Higher packet levels cannot raise it.

events.pick: Shuffle and take the first type
events.bonusPool: Build the bonus pool: cost at most 100
events.bonusPick: Choose a bonus plant on the same stream
events.remove: Set the original plant’s health to zero

eventText.ready: The center plant, price, conditions, and check inputs can be changed before replaying.
eventText.trigger: The base trigger writes clock + cooldown before any target is examined.
eventText.collect: The collector uses rectangle overlap. Targets are visited in the supplied order.
eventText.skip: This branch creates no replacement effect and consumes no shuffle outputs.
eventText.pool: The pool keeps its input order while applying type, cost, stage, planting, and blacklist gates.
eventText.pick: The complete forward shuffle runs. Its first element becomes the replacement type.
eventText.queued: The effect stores the selected type, cell, original level, and old-plant reference. The old plant remains on the board.
eventText.bonusStart: All replacement effects are still pending. The rank-4 scan sees the original board.
eventText.bonusOutside: The bonus pass checks the board bounds for each cell.
eventText.bonusOccupied: The pending replacement has not removed the occupant. This cell receives no bonus effect.
eventText.bonusPool: Bonus selection uses its own cost ceiling and planting check. It does not use the source-cost comparison.
eventText.bonusPick: The bonus shuffle continues where the earlier shuffles stopped.
eventText.bonusQueued: The grownew event will add a plant without removing an old one.
eventText.callback: The supplied callback schedule determines which pending effect runs next. No new shuffle occurs here.
eventText.remove: The loop handler tags the old plant and sets its health to zero before checking the replacement.
eventText.check: The final check uses the supplied blocking reasons without the selection-time exception.
eventText.added: The selected type is added at the stored cell and level.
eventText.failed: No AddPlant follows. A removed source is not restored.
eventText.complete: The board now contains the results of the delivered effects. Skipped targets remain unchanged.

evolution.gridInputs: Active plant anchors · planting results come from the selected input case.
evolution.guidedPlayback: Follow the main stages and one queued effect. Inspect any cell to see its selection.
evolution.detailedPlayback: Step through every target, bonus cell, and queued effect.

summaryText.selection: Targets with surviving candidates have chosen a result on the shared stream. Each effect stores that choice; the original plant is still present. Targets with an empty pool stay unchanged.
summaryText.bonus: The scan queues bonus plants for eligible empty cells, continuing the same stream. Replacement effects have not removed any originals yet.
